accepted.reason: git always closes a hunk header with @@, so a header has at least three fields and never exactly two
listing only asks whether the epoch moved since it read it; a decrement moves it just as surely, and it never returns to an earlier value
without SkipDir the walk descends into the excluded directory, but every entry below it is excluded too; skipping only saves the walk

in walkIgnored, also checking the input itself narrows its paths to the input only when git lists the input, and then everything listed below it is skipped as held anyway; the same line in reach is killed by tests of file inputs

accepted.reason: gremlins runs on Linux, where no declared path resolves under another spelling, so spelledExactly never fails there; TestMisspelledInputIsRejected covers the rejection on case-insensitive filesystems
a lone "-" selects no code whether it is read as the pattern "-" or as turning off the empty pattern
the capacity is only a preallocation hint; append grows the slice either way
the retry interval only paces polling for the lock; a zero interval polls without pausing but takes the lock as soon as it is released, as before
mutable drops testdata and vendor paths itself and .git holds no Go files, so skipping these directories only saves the walk
a reference starting with a slash names no check whether it is split or not, and the error quotes the whole reference either way
ShellCheck codes start at SC1000, so rejecting a code of exactly 1 as well changes nothing a real report can contain; the line bound on the same condition is tested
only a modification time exactly racyWindow before the hash, to the nanosecond, tells < from <=; no test can arrange that
a memo that fits one shard then records a count of one instead of omitting it, and prepare reads no further shard for either
